newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WAPET says oil output resumes after cyclone.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WAPET says oil output resumes after cyclone.

text.p: Oil production at the Barrow and Thevenard island oil fields has resumed after being shut for one day due to cyclone Rachel, which tore down the northern coast of Western Australia this week, a spokesman for the operator of the fields, West Australia Petroleum Pty Ltd (WAPET) said.
The shut-downs resulted in deferred production of about 11,000 barrels of crude from Barrow and 35,000 barrels from Thevenard, a WAPET spokesman said on Wednesday.
At its strongest Rachel recorded wind gusts of about 180 km an hour and caused the loss of over 200,000 barrels of crude oil production a day throughout the Western Australia oil patch.
The cyclone has been downgraded by weather authorities to a rain-bearing depression after reaching land on Wednesday.
WAPET is a joint venture of Texaco Inc, Chevron Inc and Royal Dutch/Shell Group, each with two-sevenths stakes, and Mobil Corp, with one-seventh.
